title: Corepressors SsnF and RcoA Regulate Development and Aflatoxin B(1) Biosynthesis in Aspergillus flavus NRRL 3357.
authors: Ma, Xiaoyun; Jiang, Yiran; Ma, Longxue; Luo, Shujuan; Du, Haolan; Li, Xu; Xing, Fuguo
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄曲霉中SsnF和RcoA共抑制因子对发育及黄曲霉毒素合成的调控，虽涉及蛋白互作对接模拟，但核心为基因表达与表型实验，非TF-DNA结合机制或AI/物理模拟方法研究。
abstract: Aspergillus flavus is a saprophytic fungus that can be found across the entire world. It can produce aflatoxin B(1) (AFB(1)), which threatens human health. CreA, as the central factor in carbon catabolite repression (CCR), regulates carbon catabolism and AFB(1) biosynthesis in A. flavus. Additionally, SsnF-RcoA are recognized as the corepressors of CreA in CCR. In this study, ssnF and rcoA not only regulated the expressions of CCR factors and hydrolase genes, but also positively affected mycelia growth, conidia production, sclerotia formation, and osmotic stress response in A. flavus. More importantly, SsnF and RcoA were identified as positive regulators for AFB(1) biosynthesis, as they modulate the AF cluster genes and the relevant regulators at a transcriptional level. Additionally, the interactions of SsnF-CreA and RcoA-CreA were strong and moderate, respectively. However, the interaction of SsnF and RcoA was weak. The interaction models of CreA-SsnF, CreA-RcoA, and SsnF-RcoA were also simulated with a docking analysis. All things considered, SsnF and RcoA are not just the critical regulators of the CCR pathway, but the global regulators involving in morphological development and AFB(1) biosynthesis in A. flavus.
abstract_zh: 黄曲霉（Aspergillus flavus）是一种腐生真菌，遍布全球。它能产生黄曲霉毒素B(1)（AFB(1)），对人类健康构成威胁。CreA作为碳分解代谢物阻遏（carbon catabolite repression, CCR）的核心因子，调控黄曲霉中的碳分解代谢和AFB(1)生物合成。此外，SsnF-RcoA被认为是CCR中CreA的共抑制因子。在本研究中，ssnF和rcoA不仅调控CCR因子和水解酶基因的表达，还正向影响黄曲霉的菌丝生长、分生孢子产生、菌核形成及渗透压应激反应。更重要的是，SsnF和RcoA被鉴定为AFB(1)生物合成的正向调控因子，因为它们通过转录水平调节AF簇基因及相关调控因子。此外，SsnF-CreA和RcoA-CreA的相互作用分别表现为强和中等强度，而SsnF与RcoA之间的相互作用较弱。通过对接分析，还模拟了CreA-SsnF、CreA-RcoA和SsnF-RcoA的相互作用模型。综合来看，SsnF和RcoA不仅是CCR通路的关键调控因子，还是参与黄曲霉形态发育和AFB(1)生物合成的全局调控因子。
